subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the value of p if the lines 4x−3y=7, 2x+py+2=0 and 6x+5y−1=0 are concurrent.

steps.margin_note: First mark. Only two of the three lines are free of p, so those two are the pair that can actually be solved.
steps.memory_tip: Solve the two lines that carry no unknown first. Concurrency is then used on the third.

steps.why: A pair containing p would leave two unknowns and no way forward, so the p-free pair is the only pair worth solving; their meeting point is the single point the third line is forced through.
common_mistakes: Writing 4x − 3y = 7 as 4x − 3y + 7 = 0 and carrying a sign error.

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Concurrency puts that point on the remaining line as well, and the equation it produces has only p in it.
steps.memory_tip: Put the point into the line that carries the unknown, and solve the one equation it gives.
